gh-70 compatibility choice (triage recommended the story workflow for this; you chose quick). Which design should implement build? (a) Dual read in one PR: intake writes spec.md; every reader (storyFile, snapshot, decide intake, brief, agent-unit, record) prefers spec.md and falls back to story.md; no files are renamed, this story's own story.md stays. Risk: a collaborator on an older norn sees a newly intaken spec.md-only story as corrupt (story.md missing) until they upgrade. (b) Two releases: this PR only adds the dual read (intake still writes story.md); a follow-up issue switches intake to spec.md after this ships. (c) Migrate on tick: the holder's tick renames story.md → spec.md and commits it (a new effect touching P6/S5/T7) — wider, better as the story workflow.

implement note on gh-82: Wanted item 'make base-sync and human cheaper' was investigated, not done: the cost is ~1,900 git spawns (~18 per tick) at ~15 ms each on macOS. Reducing it is a production change to norn's git calls (and the effect transcripts); suggest a separate issue. bun test --parallel is another option, untried.

Worktree is mid-rebase, not mid-implement. The branch tip (fad8fce) had already gone implement→test→review→qa→integrate.conflict→merge, and the merge step (run 01M61M9BG73KBDVZC5CKQC6JYJ) started 'git rebase -i' onto c5d7442. The rebase stopped on conflicts in packages/cli/src/commands/{help,index,story}.ts after replaying the early commits, and that session died. With HEAD rewound to 7214c08, runs/07-story-decision-verbs/state.json on disk reads 'implement running', so the tick classified implement.died and started this implement retry (receipts 0003–0005 are untracked and contradict the branch's real state, merge running). I haven't touched anything. To unblock, a person decides: either (a) 'git rebase --abort' to get back to fad8fce, delete the stray untracked receipts 0003–0005 and the uncommitted state.json/handoff.md changes, then rerun the merge step; or (b) finish the rebase by hand. Either way, file friction: a tick should not read state.json from a worktree with a rebase in progress, and the merge step should merge instead of rebasing over norn's state commits.

integrate rebases the slice onto the story branch, and that rebase can't apply while the conflict is fixed only in a merge commit. Story branch 2751d0f (local and origin) is already merged into the slice (fead181, merge#1), so a new merge is a no-op. But git rebase drops merge commits and replays cb8cede '# gh-75/13: config list, get, set and unset' onto 2751d0f, which conflicts again in packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts (reproduced in a throwaway worktree). The slice branch is published (origin/gh-75/13-config-list-get-set-unset = a5f1f2e), so the merge step may not rebase it. To unblock, a person can do either of these: (a) let integrate merge instead of rebase, or use a rebase that keeps the resolution (git rebase --rebase-merges, or rerere); (b) allow rewriting the slice branch into a linear history on 2751d0f. For (b), the resolution is known: the story side's COMMANDS without configCommand, and NOUNS [storyNoun, runNoun, configNoun]. Friction: a merge step can't fix a conflict from a rebase-based integrate.

Read the triage findings and the recommendation in story.md (also posted on the issue). N is the issue number. Switch to a workflow: `norn workflow gh-N fix --to reproduce`, `norn workflow gh-N quick --to implement`, `norn workflow gh-N story --to refine` or `norn workflow gh-N spec --to refine`. Close: `norn approve gh-N --reason "<why>"`, then `gh issue close N --reason "not planned"`, then `norn drop gh-N` (a story at $done without a PR otherwise waits for a merge, GR6), then `git push origin --delete gh-N-<slug>` (drop pushed the story branch; the findings stay on the issue comment). Triage again: `norn approve gh-N --reject --reason "<what to look at>"`.
